sections.hypothesis: On SOL 5m in the New York open window, a bullish change of character followed by a limit buy at the fair value gap's midpoint, with a stop beyond the gap and a 4R target, beats random entries with the same stops, targets and sizing, and beats holding at the same exposure on Sharpe, after costs.
sections.rationale: Who pays, as the method claims (Craig Percoco, Luke's YouTube batch 1 S2): a change of character marks sellers giving up, and the gap left by the move is where late buyers refill, so a limit there buys from impatient sellers. Against it, honestly: the cost gate (2026-11-15) FAILED it on 17 of 18 markets and bar sizes; SOL 5m at the New York open was the one MARGINAL case (median 0.49R of costs, from stops only, not outcomes), so it is chosen on cost, which is legitimate (the gate counted 143 such setups in its year, 2024-11 to 2025-10). It is the structure family: a Percoco structure pullback was rejected on 2026-11-05 (+0.06R). Freezing this note is Luke's knowing override of the entry bar (2026-11-16).
sections.rules: choch-fvg, SOLUSDT 5m, spot, long only. Swing highs with 3 bars either side, known 3 bars later. A bullish change of character: the last known swing high is below the one before it, and a bar (the break) closes above it, one per swing high; only breaks whose bar opens from 13:00 to 16:00 UTC (New York's open in both daylight-saving states). The leg runs from the lowest low since that swing high to the break. Its most recent bullish fair value gap (bar i's low above bar i-2's high) at least 0.3 x ATR(14) wide and known by the break's close; if none is, the next bar may complete one, and the order is placed at that bar's close instead (causal: unlike the cost gate's measurement, a known gap is never passed over for the next bar's). A buy limit at the gap's midpoint resting for 6 bars (30 minutes), filled on the first bar whose low reaches it (at the open if the bar opens below it), with market-order costs; stop at bar i-2's low; target 4R from the limit; on the fill bar only the stop can end the trade (when the high came is unknown). At most 3 orders a UTC day; one trade at a time (a newer order replaces a waiting one). Costs from kestrel.toml (7.5 bps fee a side, 1 bp half-spread: a 17 bps round trip), 330 USDT, 1% risk per trade sized by the engine, capped at 100% of equity. Period 2020-08 to 2025-10, before the holdout.
sections.falsification: The full scorecard, including test 9 (beat 95% of 200 random-entry paths with the same stops, targets and sizing). The strategy places about 140 orders a year (counted from its signals, not outcomes); fewer than 30 filled trades fails test 6.
sections.parameters: swing_bars 3 (2-6), min_gap_atr_tenths 3 (1-6, i.e. 0.1-0.6 x ATR), expiry_bars 6 (3-12), target_r 4 (2-6). One run; the robustness check moves each (about 15 neighbours).
sections.costs: About 0.49R of costs a trade at the gate's median stop: the break-even win rate at 4R rises from 20% to about 30%. Up to about 140 orders a year, fewer fills. Trials: 1 run plus about 15 neighbours; random-entry paths aren't trials.
